title: No American Indian or Alaska Native students joined Early Childhood Program for 2025-26
text:
The New York State Education Department reported no American Indian or Alaska Native students were enrolled in Early Childhood Program for the 2025-26 school year, a change of NaN% from the prior year. More details are available from the New York State Education Department .
The Early Childhood Program enrolled 59 students total in the 2025-26 school year. American Indian or Alaska Native students made up 0% of the population, resulting in the highest single-ethnicity representation at the school.
The program operates within the Greenburgh Central School District, which has its administrative offices in Hartsdale.
Woodlands Middle/High School, one of five district schools, had the largest number of American Indian or Alaska Native students at that time with four enrolled.
World Population Review’s analysis found that New York’s public education system is ranked second nationally , while it holds the 31st spot for K-12 performance.
